The user then approved page v2, verbatim via Optimize: "approved. proceed." v2 keeps storage order as it is (term order): a one-word key (atom, int, float, pid, ref) is found by word equality, as BEAM does, and order is consulted only to place a new key. Atom ids are not stable, so the v1 decisions on atom order are withdrawn. Page: https://claude.ai/artifact/MmnrdprbWQMF24ejqsUaQL (/Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-map-raw-words.html); measurements https://claude.ai/artifact/KASxGisqvtZNq498dbRi8D. User direction: meet or exceed BEAM in all cases; hand-written optimal arm64 first, then make the compiler emit it. Builder: Optimize. Pass rules are judged on bench and pre-registered on the page.

Page v3 ruling (user 2026-11-18, verbatim via Optimize): "a, b approved. continue to stack." Page: https://claude.ai/artifact/MmnrdprbWQMF24ejqsUaQL

Step 3a, the runtime half (PR #760). One find(map, word, kind) returns slot + found and serves the flat, trie-leaf and struct layouts. It is used by the runtime's put/get/has-key/fetch/delete/update/replace. Removed: map_key_position, locate_key and StructMap::position. The library half (lib/map.fz searching once) moved to its own ticket, which is blocked on the pinned-key pattern.

comments.text: Optimize's finding from .5's probes (#750): a single ordered search (kind rank, then the atom-name prefix) is within about 10% of scan-by-equality on lookups and cheaper on builds. So .7 may be one ordered search instead of scan + place. Optimize decides inside .7 with fz numbers.

title: Every map operation in the runtime finds its key with one find
